newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt names fund manager to head stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: Egypt names fund manager to head stock exchange.

text.p: Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri on Tuesday appointed a Canadian-educated fund manager as head of the Egyptian stock market, an official said.
The new chairman is Sherif Wahid Raafat, 51, a director of Concord International brokerage in Egypt, the head of the Capital Markets Authority, Abdel Hamid Ibrahim, told Reuters.
He started his career in the mid-1970s with major U.S. brokerage firms such as Kidder Peabody and Moseley, he added.
"We have succeeded in recruiting an excellent expert with local and international experience," Ibrahim said.
Raafat starts his duties on Tuesday, replacing former head Abdulghani Gamie, Ibrahim said. Gamie, who only started his job in March, resigned for health reasons, he added.
He took a master's degree in finance in 1974 at McGill University in Montreal, Canada, the CMA head added.
The Egyptian stock market includes the Cairo and Alexandria bourses.
